title: Herbaceous Hushed Filipino Rice Noodles Halo-Halo
description: A light, roasted noodle salad that captures the spirit of halo-halo with a fresh herbal twist and a hint of Filipino flavor.
instructions: Preheat oven to 400F and slice sweet potato and bell pepper into 1-inch cubes.
Toss the cubed sweet potato and bell pepper with 1 tbsp toasted sesame oil, salt, pepper, and roast for 20 minutes until caramelized.
While the vegetables roast, heat a nonstick pan over medium heat and stir-fry the cubed tofu in 2 tbsp sesame oil until golden, then set aside.
In a separate pot, bring water to a boil and cook the flat rice noodles according to package instructions until al dente, then drain and rinse with cold water.
Mince the garlic and ginger, and finely chop the scallions, reserving the green parts for garnish.
Add the minced garlic and ginger to the pot of noodles, stir-fry for 1 minute to release aroma, then pour in 3 tbsp kosher soy sauce and stir to coat.
Fold in the roasted sweet potato, bell pepper, and tofu into the noodle mixture and heat through for 2 minutes.
Finish by adding a squeeze of lime juice and a sprinkle of fresh basil, then season with salt and pepper to taste.
Divide the noodle salad into bowls and top each with the reserved scallion greens for a fresh crunch.
Serve immediately as a light, herbaceous Filipino-inspired halo-halo parody.
